text:
inc-bot: :warning: Incoming alert: widespread failures from GitHub Actions and Packages impacting org/redwood-inference workflows. Errors: artifact uploads 503, package registry timeouts. Impact: new hotfix builds blocked; automated rollouts cannot publish artifacts. Paging jamie (primary on-call).

jamie: got the page, joining Zoom. quick triage: are all repos affected or subset? which pipelines are critical for current incident?

morgan: looks org-wide — `upload-artifact` and `actions/cache` failing intermittently with 502/503. Our hotfix pipelines for service-api and infra-agent are stuck on publish steps.

devon: locally `npm publish` to registry.github.com returns 502. gh cli artifact uploads fail with `503 Service Unavailable`. build logs show `POST https://uploads.github.com/... 503`.

lee: support is seeing customers on the canaries with degraded responses; can't rollout fixes because images/packages can't be produced via GH Actions.

jamie: immediate mitigation options: 1) perform local build on bastion/dedicated runner and push images to our internal registry (artifactory.redwood). 2) create an S3-hosted npm tarball fallback for package installs. 3) promote last-known-good artifacts from our S3 artifact cache. We also need a manual approval for deploy-bot to accept non-GH artifacts.

deploy-bot: Guardrails: only artifacts signed by the `trusted-ci` key are auto-approved. To accept ad-hoc artifacts, an SRE must add an exception.

oncall-sre: I'm online. I'll open an exception window and add `incident-2026-github-registry` to allowed artifact prefixes for 2 hours. Please push with tag `hotfix-incident-1812350001`.

morgan: I'll coordinate building on a self-hosted runner. devon, can you produce npm tgz and push to s3 as `s3://redwood-temp-releases/service-core-1.2.4-hotfix.tgz`? I'll also try to build Docker image locally and push to artifactory.

devon: packing now. `npm pack` -> produced `service-core-1.2.4-hotfix.tgz`. Uploading: `aws s3 cp service-core-1.2.4-hotfix.tgz s3://redwood-temp-releases/` — upload succeeded.

morgan: building docker on self-hosted runner:
```
docker build -t artifactory.redwood/services/service-api:hotfix-1812350001 .
docker push artifactory.redwood/services/service-api:hotfix-1812350001
```
push failed first attempt (timeout), retrying on a different runner — success on runner-7.

jamie: good. next: who will update canary manifests? we need to point the canaries to the artifactory image and to use the S3 npm tarball for any build-time installs in the runtime init steps. Also update manifests so CI gating doesn't reject the deployment.

lee: I'll patch the canary deployment in us-west-2 and eu-central. steps: `kubectl -n canary set image ...` and `kubectl rollout status`. prepping command now.

lee: rollout started. pods replacing; health checks passing. latency trending back toward baseline.

sara: Customer Success notified impacted customers. Message drafted: "We're mitigating an issue caused by a third-party outage (GitHub Actions/Packages). We've deployed a manual hotfix using our internal artifact registry and will update in 2 hours or when GH resolves."

jamie: put a note in incident timeline: cause = third-party (GitHub). mitigation = manual build & artifactory promotion + S3 npm fallback. action: change deploy guard for incident-2026-github-registry. devon, leave the S3 tarball available and log the URL in the incident.

devon: S3 path `s3://redwood-temp-releases/service-core-1.2.4-hotfix.tgz` logged. Also copied the built artifacts to `s3://redwood-backups/artifacts/last-good/service-api/`.

morgan: deploy-bot exception added by oncall-sre. I verified deploy UI shows `hotfix-incident-1812350001` approval. Proceeding to complete manual canary verification. Running smoke tests.

morgan: smoke tests green on canaries. I'm going to promote hotfix to a partial rollout to additional clusters. will keep rollback plan ready.

jamie: handing off. I need to go to another priority task. morgan will take over command of this channel and the PD escalation. handoff checklist: 1) deploy gate ID `incident-2026-github-registry` active until 2026-03-XXTxx:xxZ or until GH status cleared; 2) artifactory tags: `hotfix-incident-1812350001`; 3) S3 fallback urls; 4) follow-up ticket to infra to add runbook entries and perform a drill.

morgan: taking lead. jamie paste any remaining notes and approvals here.

jamie: approvals: manual artifact acceptance granted by oncall-sre. Confirmed artifactory push and S3 path. Monitors to watch: `deploys-canary`, `service-errors`, `build-pipeline-failures`. Recovery criteria: GH Actions/Packages return to Healthy on https://www.githubstatus.com and a successful GH Actions publish from a single repo. After validation, we should re-enable GH packages and revoke the manual gate. Postmortem owners: infra (runbooks), devex (CI template changes).

morgan: noted. status updates every 20 minutes. Next: try a single guarded GH Actions run in a non-prod repo to test package publish once status is green.

inc-bot: GitHub status: Actions - Partial Outage; Packages - Degraded Performance. Link: https://www.githubstatus.com/

sara: CSMs updated customers. I'll schedule follow-up comms after root cause confirmed.

devon: follow-up: create ticket INFRA-987 to add alternate artifact publish path and document steps (S3/artifactory) into incident playbook. Also add a checklist to test the manual approval flow quarterly.

lee: Can confirm canary stability after hotfix. no further customer escalations in last 10 minutes.

morgan: taking PD now. closing this immediate build-blocking action. will keep channel open for recovery and final close.

jamie: thanks team. stepping off.

morgan: confirmed takeover. updating timeline and closing loop when GH recovers."
